thread:
incident-bot: PROD ALERT — deploy-canary-2026-03-15 failing: migration txn stuck on primary, elevated 2xx ago. Pager escalation to platform-oncall.
maya: seeing 500s from canary in eu-west for /v1/generate. Rolling error-rate to 2.1% across hosts, p95 latency +1200ms. Paging.
sandeep: on it. quick status: canary traffic (~3% of traffic) got the new schema change that adds 'session_id' (nullable) and creates a partitioned index. logs show CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY stuck behind long transaction: "waiting for lock on relation".
irene: confirmed in pg_stat_activity: backend 51234 has open tx since 10:12, client=deploy-agent, query=ALTER TABLE app.requests ADD COLUMN session_id text; and there's an index build process 51278 in state 'waiting'.
kristen: customer impact note: Support reports 8 customers seeing API 500s, internal dashboard shows 2% of generation requests failing, retries causing downstream queueing.
maya: mitigation options: 1) kill migration txn -> risk partial schema state, 2) feature-flag kill-switch to route canary back to old model, 3) rollback canary deploy entirely. Thoughts?
sandeep: killing the long tx first to unblock index build. but index build may still need to run; concurrent index might still cause locks. prefer immediate feature-flag flip to stop canary traffic, then assess DB.
kristen: agree. flip FF then escalate DB team for safe rollback/cleanup. telling support to notify impacted customers: transient 500s, short window, engineers working.
maya: executing feature-flag kill for canary route: `ffctl set canary_deploy_enabled false --env prod --scope eu-west` — doing now.
deploy-bot: feature flag change recorded: canary_deploy_enabled=false by maya at 2026-03-15T10:19:23Z. Traffic rerouting in progress.
incident-bot: Automations: reroute policy applied, canary traffic -> stable pool. Monitor: 30s.
maya: metrics after FF flip: error-rate on /v1/generate back to baseline 0.15% within 45s. p95 latency normalizing. Good so far.
sandeep: DB side: we still have the long tx (pid 51234). I can attempt to cancel it gracefully: `SELECT pg_cancel_backend(51234);` if no response, `pg_terminate_backend(51234);`.
irene: attempting cancel now.
(30s pause)
irene: cancel returned false, terminate now: `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(51234);` terminated — lock released. index process 51278 restarted and completed: "CREATE INDEX COMPLETED".
sandeep: confirmed: no further waiting_locks, replication lag normal. but because the ALTER TABLE had started then killed, the schema might be inconsistent on some replicas: running schema-check script.
kristen: support update: emailed affected customers with advisory. Ticket #INC-2026-238 opened with template.
maya: on-call handoff: I'm about to go offline in 40m; leaving notes and escalation to night oncall nate. @nate please accept handoff: issue: canary caused long migration txn, feature flag flipped, DB tx terminated, index built, stable traffic restored. Current action items: run schema-check across read replicas, confirm no partial columns on any node, follow cleanup playbook if partial DDL detected, and coordinate postmortem.
nate: taking handoff. I'm oncall for next 12h. will start by running `scripts/db/schema_check.sh --hosts prod` and ping if I see drift.
sandeep: also creating follow-up PR to move index build to offline window and to avoid CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY during canary. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5543
incident-bot: severity: sev2. Incident status: mitigated (traffic restored). Timeline saved to /incidents/3387654321/timeline. Pager will remain open until postmortem completed.
kristen: we should schedule a quick blameless postmortem: root cause hypothesis: deploy pipeline ran DDL in canary without pre-checks (concurrent tx), long-running migration from deploy-agent held lock. Primary fix: ensure DDL that builds indexes runs out-of-band or uses maintenance window + add a pre-deploy migration-safety check.
support-ops: customer impact summary for ticket: ~8 customers, ~2% requests affected, timeframe ~10:12-10:20 UTC, retries mitigated by FF flip at 10:19. no data loss reported.
maya: closing notes: rollback not executed thanks to FF flip. recommend follow-up on rollout gating for DB DDLs and add automated detection to block DDLs during canary. handing to nate for overnight watch.
nate: acknowledged. will run checks and post findings in this thread. marking incident as mitigated but not resolved until schema-check completes.
